findings.evidence: presignGet() looked up MediaObject via findByPublicId with no tenant scoping, unlike the JWT-facing requestUpload/completeUpload which scope by caller.tenantId(). The internal endpoint relied entirely on exam-delivery's upstream entitlement check as the only tenant boundary, violating the spec's explicit NFR: "audio URLs are presigned and tenant-scoped; never enumerable across tenants."
findings.why_it_matters: A compromised or buggy caller holding the internal service-key could request a presigned URL for another tenant's audio by publicId alone — single point of failure with no defense in depth at the data layer.
findings.required_action: Added tenantId as a required parameter through the full chain: PresignService.presignGet(mediaPublicId, ttlSeconds, tenantId) now uses findByPublicIdAndTenantId; InternalMediaController accepts tenantId as a query param; exam-delivery's MediaClient.presignGet passes it through; SnapshotPinService supplies entitlement.tenantId() (already available at the call site) instead of nothing.
